questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

It is not possible to discuss anything with her because of her angry.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1, i.e., because of her angry.**

The sentence uses the __incorrect adjective form__ **'angry**', which must be used along with some other noun, such as angry man etc.

Given the context of the sentence, which directly refers to it, __the word should be present in its noun form__, viz., **anger**.

Thus, the rectified sentence is: It is not possible to discuss anything with her **because of her anger.**

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

Every book __is wrote__ by Ruskin Bond is a masterpiece.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"written". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The original sentence, **"Every book is wrote by Ruskin Bond is a masterpiece," **is grammatically incorrect.
 
• The verb **"wrote" **is in the past tense, but it should be in the present tense to agree with the subject **"Every book."**
 
• Option 3, "written," is the correct answer.
 
 
• It is the past participle of the verb "write," and it can be used as an adjective to describe a noun.
 
• In this case, it is used to describe the noun "book."
 
 
 
• Therefore, the best way to improve the sentence is to replace the underlined segment with "written."
 
• The corrected sentence is: Every book written by Ruskin Bond is a masterpiece.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 3".**

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank and make a meaningful sentence.**

The Middle-East job market has always been a _______ destination for Indians.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2, i.e., lucrative.**

The sentence suggests that the __blank must contain an adjective that is appropriate for the noun 'Middle-Eastern job market'.__

Now, job markets cannot be costly, wealthy or luxury. __They signify opportunities which attract__, which is only reflected by '**lucrative**'.

Thus, the completed sentence is: The Middle-East job market has always been a lucrative destination for Indians.

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

Kaira has upset with me since the accident.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Kaira has upset". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence does not give the contextual meaning. 
 
• This sentence will be in passive form. Here been will be used after has. 
 
• Auxiliary verb, **has**, here, should be used with the past participle form of 'to be__', viz, **has been upset** (if using present perfect tense).
 
• Other correct verbs here would be simple present **'is upset**' or simple past tense verb '**was upset'**.
 
• The correct sentence is: Kaira has been upset with me since the accident. 

Hence, the correct answer is** "Option 2". **

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

Patralekha finished the cake in the blink of a eye.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1, i.e., of a eye**

The sentence uses the__ incorrect article '**a**' for the noun '**eye**'.__

Since the noun '**eye**' begins with the vowel '**e**', it necessitates the use of the** article 'an'**.

Thus, the correct part is: **of an eye**
